sections.title: Executive investment summary: a German-controlled pump franchise trading on an option it has not yet monetised

subsections.title: What the company actually does, in plain terms

blocks.text: KSB Limited manufactures centrifugal pumps, industrial valves and the spare parts and services that go with them, and sells them into six disclosed market areas: Energy, Water, General Industry, Petrochemicals and Chemicals, Building Services and Mining [F] (AR2025 p.38). It was incorporated in 1960, is headquartered at Pimpri, Pune, and operates six manufacturing plants in Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu [F] (AR2025 p.50). It is a subsidiary of the global KSB group: Canadian Kay Pump Ltd holds 40.54% and Indian promoter entities a further 29.26%, for total promoter holding of 69.80% [F] (AR2025 p.54). The Managing Director holds office as a nominee of Canadian Kay Pump Ltd [F] (AR2025 p.43).

**The company reports on a January-December calendar year, not an Indian April-March fiscal year** [F] (AR2025 p.50). Throughout this report CY2025 means the twelve months to 31 December 2025, and the latest reported period is the quarter ended June 2026, which the company calls Q2 CY2026 [F] (NUMBERS; CALL Aug 2026). This matters: the 'Q1 FY27' framing used elsewhere does not correspond to any period the company reports.

blocks.text: Customers are industrial and institutional, not consumer: EPC contractors (Larsen and Toubro, BHEL, Megha Engineering), process owners (Reliance, Tata Steel, ArcelorMittal, Hindalco, JSW), utilities and PSUs (NPCIL, ONGC, GAIL, Numaligarh Refinery), water companies (Wabag, Veolia, Voith), builders and consultants (DLF, Voltas, Shapoorji), state governments for solar irrigation (MSEDCL, TREDA, Haryana Renewable) and group companies for exports [F] (AR2025 p.7; CALL Nov 2025; AR2025 p.181). **No individual customer contributed more than 10% of group revenue in CY2025 or CY2024** [F] (AR2025 p.245).

The company is not a recent listing. Equity has been listed on BSE since 1977 and NSE since 1995, and this was the 66th annual general meeting [F] (PPT Aug 2026; AR2025 p.1). The evidence base is therefore a mature one: a full audited annual report, four institutional investor meet transcripts and a detailed investor presentation. There is no prospectus, and none was available in this folder; the ICRA rating document supplied contains only a subscriber login page and no rationale text, so the rating commentary itself could not be read [F] (RATING).

blocks.text: Classifying the drivers: **structural** - nuclear localisation policy, water and wastewater spend, aftermarket mix, group technology transfer; **company-specific** - the primary coolant pump approval, the 3-star Shirwal rating, the BP and CL technology acquisition, the FM/UL firefighting listing; **cyclical** - thermal power ordering, petrochemical capex, agricultural and solar-irrigation demand which management itself described as monsoon-dependent and scheme-dependent [AI] (CALL Nov 2025; CALL Mar 2026).

subsections.title: Bear thesis: the strongest reasons not to own it

items: **1. The price is disconnected from every valuation anchor available.** The shares trade at 56.8x trailing earnings, 40.3x EV/EBITDA and 8.24x book against a base-case DCF value of Rs 116.8 per share, implying -85.5% from the current Rs 803 [F] (NUMBERS). The reverse DCF says the price requires about 92.9% annual sales growth for five years against 12% in the base case [F] (NUMBERS).

**2. Growth has stopped.** H1 CY2026 revenue of Rs 1,292 crore was up only about 2.4% on H1 CY2025, EBITDA fell about 16% and profit after tax about 20% [E] (NUMBERS). Quarterly PAT was down 23.1% in Mar-26 and 18.6% in Jun-26 year on year [F] (NUMBERS). Management conceded sales 'hardly grew 2% to 3%' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

**3. Domestic revenue barely moved in CY2025.** Revenue within India grew 2.0%, from INR 21,700.34 Mn to INR 22,130.58 Mn; essentially all of the CY2025 growth came from exports [F] (AR2025 p.228) [E]. The headline 6.4% consolidated sales growth flatters the domestic franchise.

**4. Profit is not turning into cash.** Operating cash flow was 0.34x reported profit in CY2025, 0.58x over three years and 0.49x over five [F] (NUMBERS). Free cash flow was approximately zero in CY2025, and cumulative five-year free cash flow of Rs 95 crore compares with cumulative five-year reported profit of Rs 1,058 crore [E] (NUMBERS).

**5. Working capital is deteriorating, not normalising.** Debtor days rose to 118 from a prior three-year average of 85; the cash conversion cycle lengthened to 204 days from 163; working-capital days went to 104 from 83 [F] (NUMBERS). Work-in-progress inventory rose 45% to INR 4,276.33 Mn [F] (AR2025 p.220). Management attributes this to solar receivables from state governments and to export goods awaiting clearance [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

**6. Nearly half the order book sits in a segment that has produced almost no revenue for eight years.** Nuclear orders on hand were about Rs 1,313 crore at Jun-26 against total orders on hand of Rs 2,744 crore [F] (PPT Aug 2026), yet CY2025 nuclear revenue was 'hardly anything, Rs 30 crores to Rs 50 crores' [MC] (CALL Mar 2026). Delivery is gated by an NPCIL-built test bed the company does not control [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

**7. The test-bed slippage has now run four consecutive quarters.** August 2025: two pumps to be invoiced in CY2025 subject to test-bed readiness [MC] (CALL Sep 2025). November 2025: pumps should start 'next month or first half of January' [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). March 2026: testing to begin 22 March, two to four pumps invoiceable in the year [MC] (CALL Mar 2026). August 2026: testing had not restarted; issues in NPCIL equipment 'not yet been solved', expected September [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

**8. Management itself caps the margin.** The stated ambition is an EBITDA of 13-14%, with an explicit preference for top-line over margin: 'we wouldn't see EBITDA margins of 15%, 16%, no' [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). The 2030 aspiration is a 12-13% return on sales [F] (PPT Aug 2026). H1 CY2026 ran at about 10.3% on our statements data [E] (NUMBERS).

**9. Input-cost pass-through is partial and slow.** Foundries were given price increases of 12-15% while KSB's own price increases to standard markets remained single-digit, with a 3-6 month lag before pass-through reaches the books; project contracts are fixed-price and only about 3% of turnover carries a price-variation clause [MC] (CALL Aug 2026; CALL Mar 2026).

**10. The crown jewel is being deliberately contested.** NPCIL is developing alternative primary coolant pump suppliers and has already placed a development order with a competitor [MC] (CALL Sep 2025; CALL Mar 2026). Management's answer is experience, not exclusivity: 'What NPCIL will do, I think we can't say. It is finally left to them' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

**11. Structural dependence on the parent runs both ways.** 12.50% of sales are to related parties [F] (AR2025 p.77); the parent sets 'a general guideline' on which territories and products India may export [MC] (CALL Aug 2026); an S/4HANA cost allocation from the group will hit operating expense next year in an amount management declined to quantify [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

**12. Disclosure gaps are material for a company of this size.** No installed capacity or utilisation figures appear anywhere in the annual report; segment reporting stops at Pumps and Valves; nuclear, solar, SupremeServ and export margins are not disclosed; and the 2030 sales aspiration slide prints the 2025 actual but leaves the 2027 and 2030 target values blank [F] (AR2025 p.244; PPT Aug 2026).

The backlog has been broadly flat for two years (INR 12,354 Mn at Dec-24 to INR 13,131 Mn at Jun-26) and converted almost nothing to revenue; management guides to one pump a quarter, maximum six a year, once testing clears [F] (PPT Aug 2026) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

Debtor days have risen for three consecutive years (80, 94, 118) and the CFO said improvement would not be 'dramatic'; solar and project business are structurally more working-capital intensive than the dealer business they are displacing [F] (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)
Is the DCF wrong or is the price wrong?
A 15% WACC DCF on 13% margins cannot value a franchise with nuclear optionality [AI]

Even the bull case in our model, at 21.9% starting growth and 15% margins, values the equity at Rs 172.8 a share, 78.5% below the price; the gap is too large to be an input-assumption argument [F] (NUMBERS) [AI]
Is the parent a support or a ceiling?
Group access delivers product, references and export demand the company could never build alone [MC] (CALL Sep 2025)

The same relationship determines which markets India may serve, extracts royalty and trademark fees, and will impose an unquantified IT cost allocation; the Indian minority owns 30.20% of a business whose strategic perimeter is set abroad [F] (AR2025 p.54) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

blocks.text: Our variant perception is that the market is valuing KSB as a nuclear pure-play with an industrial cash business attached, when the evidence supports the reverse. Roughly 48% of the order book is nuclear [E] (PPT Aug 2026), but nuclear has contributed Rs 30-50 crore of revenue in its best year to date [MC] (CALL Mar 2026), sits behind a customer-owned test bed that has slipped four quarters running [MC] (CALL Aug 2026), throughputs a maximum of six pumps a year once cleared [MC] (CALL Aug 2026), and faces a customer actively qualifying a second vendor [MC] (CALL Mar 2026). Meanwhile the 98% of revenue that is not nuclear grew 2% domestically in CY2025 [E] (AR2025 p.228), carries a management-declared 13-14% margin ceiling [MC] (CALL Nov 2025), and is converting a third of its accounting profit into cash [F] (NUMBERS). The honest framing is a good, conservatively financed, technology-fed industrial compounder growing at industrial rates, priced at 56.8x earnings and 40.3x EV/EBITDA [F] (NUMBERS). The debate is not whether the business is good. It is whether any plausible nuclear outcome is large enough, soon enough, to justify what is already in the price.

blocks.text: Pofran Sales and Agency Limited has a 1 April to 31 March reporting period, different from the parent's calendar year, and the consolidation is based on unaudited financial information for the period to 31 December 2025 [F] (AR2025 p.34). The entity is financially immaterial (total assets INR 1.67 Mn), but the mismatch and the unaudited basis are worth noting as a matter of principle [AI].

KSB MIL Controls is not consolidated line-by-line because the group owns 49% and has no board control [F] (AR2025 p.34). Its contribution is meaningful to reported group profit: share of associate profit was INR 146.38 Mn of consolidated profit before tax of INR 3,604.62 Mn in CY2025, about 4.1% [F] (AR2025 p.244) [E]. KSB MIL is also a supplier and customer: purchases of INR 173.25 Mn and dividend income of INR 67.25 Mn in CY2025 [F] (AR2025 p.181).

The nuclear relationship is 49 years old and the pump business 66 years old, so this is not a narrative bolted onto a young company [F] (PPT Aug 2026). **But the parts of the business the equity story now rests on are all recent.** The Shirwal energy plant that houses the nuclear and supercritical work dates from 2017; the first nuclear order came in 2018; the first indigenous primary coolant pump was made in 2025 and was still under test in August 2026; ISO 19443 came in 2024; the BP and CL reciprocating-pump technology arrived in 2022-23; the firefighting FM/UL listing, the vertical turbine pump, the mining white-iron casting capability, the marine NAB castings and the solar controller were all completed in 2024-2025 [F] (AR2025 p.11-13; PPT Aug 2026).

Read forensically, the company has spent roughly a decade building capability and has not yet been paid for most of it [AI]. Revenue compounded 14% over nine years and 17.4% over five, but the last twelve months grew 1.1% over the last full year [F] (NUMBERS). The timeline is the story of an option portfolio being assembled; the income statement has not yet recorded the exercise [AI].

sections.title: How the business is built and where the value is actually captured

subsections.title: The production and service chain, step by step

items: **1. Design and hydraulics.** Pump hydraulics and metallurgy are designed by KSB SE in Germany; KSB India absorbs and localises technology under licence, paying royalty, technical-service and trademark fees [F] (AR2025 p.111, p.181). For the Kudankulam safety package the adaptation engineering was done in India because the pumps had originally been planned from Ukraine [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

**2. Castings.** Captive foundry at Vambori supplies ferrous and non-ferrous castings; NORSOK certification for offshore and oil-and-gas, white iron for mining wear parts, nickel-aluminium bronze for marine, electropolishing for desalination duplex stainless [F] (AR2025 p.5, p.13). Third-party foundries supply the balance; both are gas-fired and were disrupted by LPG and gas supply restrictions [MC] (CALL Mar 2026).

**3. Machining and fabrication.** In-house machining across Pimpri (industrial pumps), Sinnar (standard/water pumps), Shirwal (energy, nuclear, oil and gas) and Coimbatore (valves); recent additions include a Mazak 5-axis CNC machine, robotic diode laser cladding for valve seats and a hybrid valve assembly line [F] (AR2025 p.7, p.8, p.13).

**4. Assembly and testing.** Shirwal has a digitised test bed and dedicated bays, plus a nuclear mechanical-seal dynamic testing facility [F] (AR2025 p.9; PPT Aug 2026). Critical nuclear pumps must additionally pass a 500-hour endurance test on a customer-owned test bed at Tarapur, which is not in the company's control [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

**5. Qualification and approvals.** This is a gate, not a step: ISO 19443 for nuclear, ASME Section III NB, FM and UL for firefighting, API Monogram targeted for 2026 valves, EIL approval for reciprocating pumps requiring a pump running in service for 12 months, naval type-testing for marine, MNRE certification for solar [F] (AR2025 p.12) [MC] (CALL Nov 2025; CALL Aug 2026).

**6. Route to market.** Roughly half the business goes through 800+ authorised dealers and 1,167 distributors; the balance goes direct to EPCs, OEMs and end users; exports transact 70-80% inter-company through KSB group entities [F] (AR2025 p.77; PPT Aug 2026) [MC] (CALL Mar 2026).

**7. Aftermarket.** Once installed, pumps are tracked in a C4C CRM by serial number and pump type, and served through 350+ authorised service centres, six in-house repair centres, 40+ field service engineers, a 2,500 sq m central spares warehouse with 14,000 bin locations, reverse engineering with 3D scanning, mechanical seal manufacture and repair, boiler-circulation pump rewinding and digital monitoring products (KSB Guard, Sonolyzer) [F] (AR2025 p.7) [MC] (CALL Nov 2025).

subsections.title: Where value is captured, and why

blocks.text: Value is captured in three places, in descending order of quality per rupee of revenue. First, **aftermarket spares and services**, where gross margins are described as two to three times new-pump margins and the customer negotiates on availability rather than price: 'if a mechanical seal is leaking, he will not negotiate the price' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026; CALL Mar 2026). Second, **standard dealer and OEM pumps**, about half the business, where low fixed cost, fast turnover and a distribution channel produce good profitability and good cash flow [MC] (CALL Mar 2026). Third, **engineered and project pumps**, which management explicitly identifies as the competitive, price-pressured end: refinery, petrochemical, API and coal-fired thermal, where 'everybody is focused and desperate to fill up their plants' [MC] (CALL Mar 2026). The VP Sales went further and directly contradicted the common assumption: 'I disagree with your point that engineered pump business is more profitable business' [MC] (CALL Nov 2025).

The disclosed segment data supports this only partially. In CY2025 Pumps earned a segment margin of about 12.9% and Valves about 14.5%; in CY2024 the figures were about 11.0% and 15.2% [E] (AR2025 p.244). So the smaller, more commoditised-sounding valves business has consistently earned the better segment margin, and the pumps segment - which contains nuclear, solar, standard and aftermarket all mixed together - improved in CY2025 while valves declined [AI]. The company does not break Pumps down further, so the aftermarket margin claim cannot be verified from the statements [F] (AR2025 p.244).

Strategic orders are taken at depressed margins on purpose: 'you would definitely compromise on those margins, because you have a long-term strategy' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). That is a defensible installed-base strategy, but it means reported margin in any given year is partly a policy choice and partly mix, and an outside analyst cannot separate the two from disclosure [AI].

The model is moderately capital-intensive and becoming less so per rupee of sales. Capex was Rs 93 crore in CY2025, 3.4% of sales, against 5.8% in 2022; fixed-asset turnover improved from 3.77x in 2016 to 5.84x in 2025 [F] (NUMBERS). Gross block stood at INR 11,485 Mn against net block of INR 5,535 Mn, so the asset base is roughly half depreciated [F] (AR2025 p.40) [E]. Capital work-in-progress nearly doubled to INR 888.91 Mn, and capital commitments not provided for were INR 395.97 Mn [F] (AR2025 p.197, p.169).

The bought-out content is substantial: purchases of stock-in-trade were INR 2,748.95 Mn in CY2025 on top of INR 12,745.93 Mn of materials consumed [F] (AR2025 p.229). subsections.title: Is the export mix strategy or mix?

blocks.text: It is strategy, but strategy executed inside a group allocation system, which is a different thing from an independent export franchise [AI]. Management is explicit: 'the parents only makes a guideline that which territories and which products you're allowed to export... they balance the loading of all factories globally' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Transactions are 70-80% inter-company [MC] (CALL Mar 2026), and sales to related parties were 12.50% of total sales in CY2025 [F] (AR2025 p.77), against exports of 17.4% - so the majority of export revenue is billed to sister companies [E].

The counter-argument, which we accept as genuine, is that KSB India has been earning a larger allocation. The MD says the ground sales effort is '100%' the Indian entity's, that the parent does not participate operatively, and that the Shirwal 3-star Made-by-KSB rating - held by only three of roughly 35 group sites - raises acceptance inside the group [MC] (CALL Aug 2026; CALL Sep 2025). KSB India is also designated the sole group manufacturing entity for VMD mining pumps [F] (AR2025 p.12). Target: exports at 20% of sales, versus management's own estimate of about 15% currently [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

items: Foreign exchange earned in CY2025 was INR 4,403.70 Mn against foreign exchange used of INR 1,500.02 Mn, so the company is structurally a net FX earner [F] (AR2025 p.111).

Net gain on foreign currency transactions and translations was INR 177.02 Mn in CY2025, up from INR 63.62 Mn, contributing about 5% of profit before tax [F] (AR2025 p.229) [E]. This is a real but volatile earnings contributor and should not be read as operating performance [AI].

Derivatives are used and carried at fair value through profit or loss; the fair value of derivative instruments is determined at forward rates and the deferred tax note carries a fair-value loss on derivatives, so hedging is active but the hedge ratio is not disclosed [F] (AR2025 p.183, p.222).

**US tariffs:** 'we went there, then the tariffs came, and then some orders got cancelled'; the company won USD 5-7 million of gas-power boiler feed pump orders and an approximately equal amount was cancelled because of tariffs. By March 2026 the MD said 'with the tariff back at same level as others, we are back in contention' [MC] (CALL Mar 2026).

**Middle East conflict:** disrupted shipments and blocked finished exports through H1 CY2026; management said in August 2026 that exports had 'not yet' come back on track [MC] (CALL Aug 2026; CALL Mar 2026).

**India-EU FTA:** management expects little export benefit because European import duties are already negligible, but sees an opportunity to import parent products (circulator pumps, IE5 motors, automation) where the current landed cost penalty is 15-20% including surcharges [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Note this would increase, not decrease, purchases from the parent [AI].

**Nuclear trade policy:** the SHANTI Act permitting private participation is cited as the key enabler; management believes nuclear will remain a Make-in-India localisation requirement rather than an import opening [F] (AR2025 p.36) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

blocks.text: The company is not single-location in aggregate: six plants across Pimpri, Chinchwad, Vambori, Sinnar, Kesurdi (Shirwal) and NSN Palayam (Coimbatore) [F] (AR2025 p.50). **But it is single-location where it matters most.** All nuclear and energy pump manufacture, testing and the nuclear mechanical-seal facility sit at Shirwal [F] (AR2025 p.13; PPT Aug 2026); all valves at Coimbatore plus control valves at the associate's Meladoor plant [F] (AR2025 p.50); all captive castings at Vambori [F] (AR2025 p.13); all aftermarket, seal manufacture, reverse engineering and central warehousing at Chinchwad [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). Five of the six plants are in a single state, Maharashtra [F] (AR2025 p.50). A prolonged interruption at Shirwal or Vambori would be difficult to route around, and the CY2026 foundry gas disruption is a live demonstration of the second case [AI] (CALL Mar 2026).

subsections.title: Utilisation trend and why it changed

blocks.text: Three utilisation data points exist in the whole file. An analyst in November 2025 referred back to a first-quarter management statement that the company was 'operating at close to 85% kind of utilization', and the MD did not dispute it, answering instead on debottlenecking [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). In August 2026 the COO Nuclear said of Shirwal that the additional shed 'will give us a comfort that we are already at 80% to 90% capacity utilization' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). And the MD has said repeatedly that internal efficiency has raised output on unchanged plant: 'the same plants, which we're delivering X turnover, now they are doing 2x turnovers' [MC] (CALL Nov 2025).

The supporting evidence for that last claim is in the ratios, not in a capacity table: **fixed-asset turnover rose from 3.77x in 2016 to 5.84x in 2025**, and capex fell from 9.6% of sales in 2016 to 3.4% in 2025 [F] (NUMBERS). That is a genuine and sustained efficiency gain. It is also the reason management has resisted a large capacity programme: 'let's try to see how much we can extract more out of our things... The question of further land and everything, I think it is in discussion, but nothing decided yet' [MC] (CALL Nov 2025).

Utilisation changed for three disclosed reasons: throughput engineering (value stream mapping in valves, hybrid assembly line, robotic cladding, 5-axis machining) [F] (AR2025 p.8, p.13); capacity additions at Shirwal and Sinnar commissioned around March 2026 and mid-2026 [MC] (CALL Nov 2025; CALL Aug 2026); and, in the other direction, the H1 CY2026 casting supply disruption, which idled capacity the company could not feed [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

items: Shirwal runs at 1,200-1,300 pumps a year across energy, oil and gas and nuclear at 80-90% utilisation, and the new shed is stated to add about 20% capacity [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). **That cannot be converted into rupees.** The company does not disclose Shirwal revenue, nor energy division revenue, nor the average realisation per pump at that plant [F]. Any rupee figure would be fabricated [AI].

The nuclear sub-constraint is harder and is disclosed: 'We see one pump every quarter, but we can maximize this to up to six pumps per year' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). With two-unit nuclear pump scope stated at Rs 500-600 crore [MC] (CALL Sep 2025), the throughput cap, not the floor space, is what limits nuclear revenue recognition [AI].

At group level, the most defensible utilisation-linked observation is the historical one: revenue rose from Rs 1,497 crore (2021) to Rs 2,696 crore (2025), an increase of Rs 1,199 crore, against cumulative capex over the same five years of Rs 427 crore [E] (NUMBERS). The incremental sales-to-capital ratio of about 2.8x is the honest proxy for what further utilisation gains can deliver [E].

The audited source covers CY2025 and CY2024 only, in both standalone and consolidated form [F] (AR2025 p.135, p.197). **The two quarters of CY2026 in our statements data are unaudited exchange filings and are not in the annual report** [AI].

The annual report's five-year financial summary and key ratios are **standalone**, while our statements data is **consolidated**; several ratios therefore differ and we show both [F] (AR2025 p.40, p.41).

Earnings per share is not comparable across the annual report's own five-year table: CY2023 shows Rs 58.78 and CY2024 Rs 13.84 because of the sub-division of shares to a face value of Rs 2; our statements data restates the whole history on the post-split base [F] (AR2025 p.40; NUMBERS).

Ten-year segment history, capacity data and customer-level revenue do not exist in any document supplied [F].

**Growth has decelerated sharply at the end of a good decade.** Nine-year sales CAGR 14.0%, five-year 17.4%, three-year 14.0% - but trailing twelve-month sales are only 1.1% above the last full year [F] (NUMBERS).

**Total assets grew 19% to Rs 2,793 crore while sales grew 6.4%** [F] (NUMBERS). The asset base is outrunning revenue.

**Other assets - screener's catch-all for inventory, receivables, cash and other current items - are Rs 2,143 crore, 77% of the balance sheet** [F] (NUMBERS) [E]. This is a working-capital company with a factory attached [AI].
**Net fixed assets of Rs 462 crore plus CWIP of Rs 92 crore support Rs 2,696 crore of sales** [F] (NUMBERS). CWIP rose 67% year on year, consistent with the Shirwal and Sinnar sheds [AI].

subsections.title: Audit trail compliance: the one genuine qualification-adjacent finding

blocks.text: **The auditor's opinion on books of account is not clean.** Under section 143(3)(b) the auditor reports that proper books have been kept 'except that the backup of audit trail (edit log) maintained in electronic mode has not been maintained on servers physically located in India during the year' and except for the Rule 11(g) matters [F] (AR2025 p.127).

items: In the core accounting software, the audit trail is not maintained for certain information or data; at the database layer the audit trail feature has not been enabled to log direct data changes for one user, and the audit log of modifications does not contain pre-modified values [F] (AR2025 p.128).

In a second accounting software hosted by third-party service providers, the database-level audit trail was not enabled to log direct data changes up to 29 May 2025, and from 30 May 2025 the audit log of modifications does not contain pre-modified values [F] (AR2025 p.128).
The auditor did not notice any instance of the audit trail feature being tampered with, and the trail to the extent maintained in the prior year has been preserved [F] (AR2025 p.128).
The consolidated report carries the same finding on server location [F] (AR2025 p.194).

**Read:** these are compliance failures of exactly the type Rule 11(g) was written to surface - the absence of pre-modified values and an un-enabled database-layer log mean direct data changes by a privileged user would not be reconstructable [AI]. There is no evidence of misuse. But for a company of this size, with a German parent and a global IT function, it is a control gap that should have been closed, and it is scheduled to persist until the S/4HANA migration [AI] (CALL Aug 2026).

subsections.title: The two questions the scores cannot answer

items: **1. How durable is a regulatory moat when the regulator's affiliate is the one dismantling it?** KSB's nuclear position rests on being the only approved Indian supplier of primary coolant pumps [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). NPCIL is the customer, the approver and the party that has issued a development order to a competitor and states a plan 'to have more vendors, which is very normal' [MC] (CALL Mar 2026). A moat granted by a single counterparty can be revoked by that counterparty, and no score can capture the probability or the timing [AI].

**2. What is the technology licence actually worth, and to whom?** The portfolio breadth that underpins scores on technology, switching costs and approvals is licensed from KSB SE on terms set inside the group and audited through a transfer-pricing framework whose Advance Pricing Agreement for FY2018-23 was still pending seven years after filing [F] (AR2025 p.253). The scores measure the moat around the business. They cannot measure how much of the resulting economics accrues to the Indian minority rather than to the licensor [AI].

blocks.text: **Conclusion: a real, narrow, borrowed moat.** The approval barriers are genuine, multi-year and demonstrably hard to cross - competitors have been trying at NPCIL for years without qualifying [MC] (CALL Sep 2025). The aftermarket and installed base create durable, low-competition revenue that management says carries two to three times the gross margin of new pumps [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). But three qualifications matter. The moat protects the smallest revenue lines. It is licensed rather than owned. And in its deepest section - nuclear - the customer has publicly stated its intention to widen the supplier base [MC] (CALL Mar 2026). A 6.0 moat score is consistent with a durable, above-cost-of-capital business. It is not consistent with a franchise that can compound at rates far above its end markets for a decade [AI].

subsections.title: Interpreting the DCF and its assumptions

blocks.text: Three points of interpretation, and one important caveat about what a DCF can and cannot capture here [AI].

items: **The discount rate is the dominant assumption.** A 15.0% WACC built from a 7% risk-free rate, a 7% equity risk premium and a 1.15 beta is a standard Indian mid-cap construction [F] (NUMBERS). For a debt-free company with 25% ROCE, AA+ rated credit lines and a 66-year operating history, an argument exists that the beta and therefore the cost of equity are too high. The sensitivity grid quantifies that argument: dropping to 13.5% adds about 22% to the value and still leaves it 82% below the price [F] (NUMBERS) [E].

**The model does not value optionality separately.** A nuclear franchise with a 49-year qualification history, a sole-approved-supplier position and a 100 GW national programme behind it is the kind of asset a DCF on blended margins systematically under-values, because the payoff is lumpy, long-dated and binary [AI]. The counter is that management's own sizing of that option - Rs 300-400 crore of revenue in a good year at 'reasonably good' margins - is not large enough to bridge a gap of this size [MC] (CALL Mar 2026) [AI].

**The working capital assumption is a real economic charge, not an accounting artefact.** The model deducts the change in net working capital at 88 days from every rupee of incremental sales. Given the company has actually run at 104 days and has converted 49 paise of each rupee of five-year profit into operating cash, this is a fair charge, arguably a generous one [F] (NUMBERS) [E]. It is also the single biggest reason base-case FCFF of Rs 94.1 crore in year one is so much smaller than base-case EBITDA of Rs 404 crore [E].

**Caveat: the gap is too large to be an input argument.** No combination of cells in the disclosed sensitivity grid, and no scenario including the bull case, comes within 78% of the market price [F] (NUMBERS). When a model and a market disagree by this much, the useful conclusion is not that one number is right - it is that the market is valuing something the cash-flow framework does not contain, and the burden is on the buyer to say what that is and what it is worth [AI].

**The forensic conclusion is narrower and more useful than the headline number.** At Rs 803 the market is paying 40.3x EV/EBITDA for a business that: grew sales 6.4% in its last full year and 2.4% in its most recent half; converted 34 paise of each rupee of last year's profit into operating cash and 49 paise over five years; is run to a management-declared EBITDA ceiling of 13-14%; has roughly 48% of its order book in a segment that produced 1-2% of revenue; and has missed its own timing guidance on that segment four quarters running [F] (NUMBERS; AR2025 p.228; PPT Aug 2026) [E] [MC] (CALL Nov 2025; CALL Aug 2026).

Even a perfect nuclear outcome does not change the growth algorithm of a Rs 2,700 crore company by enough to justify a 92.9% implied rate, or anything approaching it [AI].

There is a second, subtler forensic point. The gap between accounting earnings and cash is what makes the multiple so punishing. A 56.8x price-earnings multiple on earnings that convert to cash at 0.49x over five years is, in cash terms, a far higher multiple than the headline suggests [F] (NUMBERS) [AI]. Until working capital stops absorbing growth, the earnings the multiple is applied to are not distributable earnings [AI].

items: **A 15% cost of equity is a high bar for a debt-free, AA+ rated, 25%-ROCE, 66-year-old franchise with a German multinational parent** [F] (NUMBERS; AR2025 p.29). KSB India is a genuinely good industrial business with a scarce asset attached. The core is 66 years old, debt-free, earns 25% on capital employed, has raised its dividend every year for five years, has never diluted, and has lifted fixed-asset turnover from 3.77x to 5.84x while cutting capex intensity from 9.6% to 3.4% of sales [F] (NUMBERS; AR2025 p.6). It sits inside a EUR 3.0 bn global group that supplies technology, export demand and a quality system that rates the Shirwal plant among the best three of about 35 sites worldwide [F] (PPT Aug 2026) [MC] (CALL Sep 2025).

The scarce asset is nuclear qualification. All Indian PHWRs after Narora run KSB primary coolant pumps; the relationship dates to a 1977 tripartite agreement with the Department of Atomic Energy; the company is the first Indian pump maker with ISO 19443; and it is today the approved supplier [F] (PPT Aug 2026) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Against a state programme targeting 22,480 MW by 2031-32 and 100 GW by 2047, with the SHANTI Act opening private participation, this is a real option on a multi-decade localisation cycle [F] (PPT Aug 2026; AR2025 p.36). Layered on top: a mandated minimum 80 GW of new coal capacity by 2031-32 where KSB has just localised the last imported pump category [F] (AR2025 p.36) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026); a Rs 8.69 lakh crore water mission into which the company has just completed its product range [F] (AR2025 p.35); exports up 33% and compounding at about 21%; and an aftermarket business at 15% of revenue earning two to three times the gross margin of new pumps [F] (AR2025 p.228; PPT Aug 2026) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

Everything above is already understood and priced several times over. At Rs 803 the shares trade at 56.8x trailing earnings, 40.3x EV/EBITDA and 8.24x book, against DCF values of Rs 51.1 bear, Rs 116.8 base and Rs 172.8 bull, and a reverse DCF requiring about 93% annual sales growth for five years [F] (NUMBERS). Meanwhile the operating record has turned: domestic revenue grew 2.0% in CY2025, H1 CY2026 revenue grew about 2.4% with profit after tax down about 20%, and the March 2026 quarter posted the lowest EBITDA margin in three years [E] (AR2025 p.228; NUMBERS).

Underneath, the cash record is poor and getting worse: 34 paise of operating cash per rupee of profit last year, 49 paise over five years, and Rs 95 crore of cumulative free cash flow against Rs 1,058 crore of cumulative profit [E] (NUMBERS). The cause is a balance sheet absorbing growth - 118 debtor days, 204 days of cash conversion cycle, work-in-progress up 45%, and overdue receivables doubling while the provision fell as a share of the book [F] (NUMBERS; AR2025 p.218-219) [E]. And the nuclear option, which carries the valuation, has slipped four consecutive quarters, is capped at six pumps a year, is sized by management at Rs 300-400 crore of revenue in a good year, and faces a customer openly qualifying a second supplier [MC] (CALL Aug 2026; CALL Mar 2026).

blocks.caption: Both sides of the argument
rows: **The non-nuclear localisation pipeline is larger and better evidenced than the nuclear story.** The first localised boiler circulation pump, descaling pumps replacing Japanese imports, reciprocating pumps via BP and CL, vertical turbine and split-case water pumps, mining white iron, marine NAB castings and FM/UL firefighting are all dated, named and order-backed - and none of them depends on NPCIL [F] (AR2025 p.7, p.11-13) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

**The aftermarket infrastructure is more built-out than the 15% revenue share suggests.** A dedicated plant, 350+ service centres, a serial-number installed-base tracker, reverse engineering, seal manufacture and repair, and boiler-circulation rewinding capability that attracts work from Malaysia and Indonesia [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) [AI]

**Working capital may prove cyclical.** The two named causes - solar documentation and blocked exports - are both identifiable and both, in principle, self-correcting; customer advances rose 50% and are not captured in the days calculation [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) [F] (AR2025 p.228)

**The nuclear option is smaller than the order book implies.** Rs 1,313 crore of backlog, a six-pump-a-year ceiling, a Rs 300-400 crore good-year revenue estimate from management itself, and primary coolant pumps designed to last 40-60 years with almost no aftermarket - 'Unfortunately, our PCPs are so good. So it's not much' [MC] (CALL Mar 2026; CALL Aug 2026; CALL Nov 2025)

**The margin ceiling is management's own policy, repeatedly restated.** Investors modelling margin expansion are modelling against the company's declared strategy of prioritising top line over margin [MC] (CALL Nov 2025; CALL Mar 2026)

**The growth mix is shifting toward lower-quality revenue.** Solar three to four points below group margin with the worst working capital; firefighting a bought-out system; engineered project work in what management calls a desperate price environment [MC] (CALL Mar 2026; CALL Nov 2025)
**Roughly 17% of pre-tax profit flows to the parent as fees**, on terms set inside the group under a transfer-pricing framework unresolved since 2018 [F] (AR2025 p.181, p.253) [E]

items: **Bear path:** sales reach Rs 3,529 crore by year five at a 9% EBITDA margin [F] (NUMBERS). In practice this looks like nuclear never converting at scale, exports staying geopolitically constrained, solar prices grinding down, and input costs never fully recovered. The business survives comfortably - it has no debt - but the equity de-rates severely [AI].

**Base path:** sales reach Rs 4,802 crore at a 13% margin [F] (NUMBERS). This is management delivering roughly what it says it will: double-digit growth, the stated margin band, the nuclear book converting over three to four years, exports at 20% of sales, SupremeServ drifting toward 20%. A good outcome for the business; still a large gap to today's price on this framework [AI].

**Bull path:** sales reach Rs 6,082 crore at a 15% margin [F] (NUMBERS). This requires the fleet tender won at scale, nuclear at the top of management's Rs 300-400 crore range, thermal ordering delivering, exports beating 20%, the aftermarket mix shift actually landing, and a margin level management has publicly declined to claim [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) [AI].

**The path that the current price implies is not in the possibility space defined by the model at all** - it requires about 93% annual sales growth, which would exceed the entire disclosed Indian centrifugal pump market within the forecast period [F] (NUMBERS; PPT Aug 2026) [AI].

subsections.title: Where the price sits against the model, and what drives the gap

blocks.text: **This report carries no rating and no price target.** The research view is as follows [AI].

The share price of Rs 803 sits 78.5% above the bull-case fair value of Rs 172.8, 85.5% above the base-case Rs 116.8 and 93.6% above the bear-case Rs 51.1 produced by our DCF model, and above every cell of the disclosed sensitivity grid, whose range is Rs 96.1 to Rs 151.3 [F] (NUMBERS).

Four things drive that gap, in order of size [AI]. First, **the discount rate**: a 15.0% WACC from a 1.15 beta and a 7% equity risk premium is a demanding hurdle for a debt-free, AA+ rated, 25%-ROCE franchise, and the sensitivity grid shows a 150 basis point reduction is worth about 22% - meaningful but nowhere near sufficient [F] (NUMBERS) [E]. Second, **free cash flow conversion inside the model**: base-case year-one FCFF of Rs 94.1 crore on EBITDA of Rs 404 crore reflects an 88-day working-capital charge on incremental sales, which is both economically fair given a 0.49x five-year cash conversion record and more generous than the 104 days actually reported [F] (NUMBERS) [E]. Third, **the absence of separately valued optionality**: a lumpy, binary, multi-decade nuclear franchise is exactly what a blended-margin DCF under-captures, although management's own revenue sizing of that option caps how much it could be worth [MC] (CALL Mar 2026) [AI]. Fourth, and most important, **the market is not discounting cash flows at all on these inputs**; at 40.3x EV/EBITDA it is paying for a structural re-rating of Indian capital goods and for a nuclear narrative whose revenue has yet to appear [AI].

The single most important finding in this report is not the valuation gap. It is that **KSB has converted 49 paise of every rupee of the last five years' reported profit into operating cash, and Rs 95 crore of Rs 1,058 crore into free cash flow** [E] (NUMBERS). A 56.8x multiple applied to earnings of that cash quality is a materially higher multiple than it appears [AI].

subsections.title: Investment-horizon guidance and when to re-review

items: **This is not a one-quarter story in either direction.** The two variables that matter - nuclear conversion and working-capital normalisation - operate on 12 to 36 month cycles. Nuclear execution is 24-48 months from order to delivery and is gated by a third party; working capital has deteriorated over three consecutive years and management has explicitly said improvement will not be 'dramatic' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Anyone underwriting this business needs a three-to-five year horizon [AI].

**Re-review trigger 1 - Q3 CY2026 results (around November 2026).** The first test of the promised second-half recovery in exports, solar and margin. Watch revenue growth against the 2.4% first half, EBITDA margin against the 13-14% band, and debtor days [F] (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

**Re-review trigger 2 - the GHAVP 500-hour test.** Any announcement that testing has started, and then that the first pump has been invoiced. Management expected a September 2026 start with a two-to-three month test [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

**Re-review trigger 3 - the NPCIL fleet tender.** Its issue, its scope (whether eight reactors), and critically whether KSB is the sole qualified bidder or faces the competitor holding the development order [MC] (CALL Aug 2026; CALL Mar 2026).

**Re-review trigger 4 - full-year CY2026 results and the CY2026 annual report (around February-April 2027).** The disclosures to test are: the cash flow statement for CFO/PAT; the receivables ageing table and the loss allowance; the inventory note for work-in-progress and write-downs; the segment note for Pumps and Valves margins; the related-party note for royalty and any first S/4HANA allocation; and the audit report for whether the audit-trail exceptions have been remediated [F] (AR2025 p.199, p.218-220, p.244, p.181, p.127-128).

**Re-review trigger 5 - any disclosure upgrade.** If the company begins publishing capacity, utilisation, or revenue for nuclear, solar, SupremeServ and exports, the entire analysis becomes materially more testable and the report should be rebuilt on it [AI].

summary.one_line: KSB Limited is a debt-free, 25%-ROCE pump and valve franchise with a genuine 49-year nuclear qualification moat, but its domestic revenue grew 2% in CY2025, H1 CY2026 profit fell about 20%, it has converted only 49 paise of every rupee of five-year profit into operating cash, and at Rs 803 it trades 78% to 94% above every fair value our DCF model produces.
bull_points: [F] (PPT Aug 2026) Sole approved Indian supplier of nuclear primary coolant pumps with a 49-year record: all PHWRs after Narora carry KSB pumps, the company is the first Indian pump maker with ISO 19443, and nuclear orders on hand are about Rs 1,313 crore against a state programme targeting 22,480 MW by 2031-32 and 100 GW by 2047.

[F] (NUMBERS; AR2025 p.29) Fortress balance sheet funding growth without dilution: borrowings of Rs 5 crore against equity of Rs 1,679 crore, debt/equity 0.00x, ROCE 25%, INR 2,833.90 Mn of cash and bank balances, an undrawn ICRA AA+ rated line of INR 25,000 Mn, no equity issued in ten years and no stock option scheme.

[F] (AR2025 p.228; PPT Aug 2026) Exports are the one line genuinely compounding: revenue up 33.3% to INR 4,665.73 Mn in CY2025 and export order intake up from INR 1,973 Mn in 2020 to INR 5,141 Mn in 2025, helped by Shirwal being one of only three KSB group sites worldwide with a 3-star Made-by-KSB rating [MC] (CALL Sep 2025).

[F] (AR2025 p.7, p.11-13) A dated, order-backed import-substitution pipeline that does not depend on NPCIL: the first localised LUV boiler circulation pump, descaling pumps replacing Japanese imports at Tata Steel, first-ever reciprocating pumps for GAIL Pata, vertical turbine and split-case water pumps, FM and UL listed firefighting pumps, and white iron and NORSOK foundry qualification.

[MC] (CALL Aug 2026) The aftermarket mix lever is real and being built: SupremeServ is about 15% of revenue with spare-part gross margins described as two to three times new-pump margins, growing 15% a year, against a stated goal of 25-30%.
bear_points: [F] (NUMBERS) Valuation is disconnected from every anchor available: 56.8x trailing earnings, 40.3x EV/EBITDA and 8.24x book against DCF values of Rs 51.1 bear, Rs 116.8 base and Rs 172.8 bull, with the reverse DCF requiring about 92.9% annual sales growth for five years versus 12.0% in the base case.
